_comment: folio-assist-core — THE CONTENT LAYER, declared as a real instance on the owner's ruling of 2026-09-20 ("Create f-a-core/ as a real instance now"). It declares NO directories, deliberately: the modules it will own are still interleaved with the harness's under cat-harness/, and declaring a directory that is not there is the dh4f defect — every consumer then scans nothing and reports a clean run over it. An instance that declares only what it has is honest; one that declares its target layout is a lie a gate cannot catch. scripts/repo-partition.ts is the machine-readable statement of what will move here.

assets.description: The layer's scope, stated as a table of what is in and out, so the boundary is checkable rather than remembered. Self-documenting on the forge: a person landing on the directory reads the thing itself.

_stickies_comment: ONE card, because the owner's ruling is one card per harness: "not all stickies should be cat harness they should be outputs (as if) each init harness ran ... each own intiaization sticky note to show sucess". This layer takes the knowledge-graph overview, which was cat-harness's third card — content is this layer's subject, so the card that explains the sub-graphs belongs to it rather than to the platform that operates on them.

stickies._comment: THEME: `library`, its own, per "each harness hould have its own unique theme (by convention)". The librarian reads: this layer is about what content IS and how it is organised. It is not cat-harness's hoodie and not bootstrap's cowboy. SCOPE is stated in the body rather than left to the reader, per "also some guidance what is its scope".
stickies.body:
The knowledge graph is four sub-graphs, and an instance declares which of them it holds.

**Content** is what somebody authors and a reader reads — this layer's subject. **Skills** are the instructions an agent follows to do the work. **Processes** are the BPMN diagrams that say who does what, in which order, and where the gates are — they are executable, not illustrations. **Tools** are what an agent can call.

Getting anything in is **acquisition**: unstructured and semi-structured sources arrive through `uploads/` or through the conversation, and are ingested into `library/`. It is a step rather than a graph kind of its own — there is no fifth directory to look for.

**Scope:** the content model — what a folio IS. Not the skills and tools that operate on it, and not any particular folio's chapters.
